query: Controlling for priority and category, which underlying causes explain longer resolution times?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: A restatement of the focus variable (resolution time) in hours; this is the outcome itself, not a candidate cause.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Priority is explicitly named in the query as something to control for. It plausibly affects both which incidents get certain treatments (e.g., staffing/routing) and resolution time, but it was copied directly from the query.

per_column.name: involves_infrastructure
per_column.rationale: A candidate underlying cause (issue type) whose effect on resolution time is being attributed. Derived from the text/data, not named in query.

per_column.name: involves_access_issue
per_column.rationale: Another candidate cause-type flag whose effect on resolution time is under attribution.

per_column.name: involves_performance
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause-type flag; a potential explanatory factor for longer resolution times.

per_column.name: involves_database
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause-type flag; potential explanatory factor for resolution time.

per_column.name: was_resolved
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident was resolved is downstream of / jointly determined with resolution time (resolution time is only defined when resolved). Conditioning on it induces selection bias; it is not a common cause.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply plausible candidate treatments (the involves_* issue-type flags) whose effects on resolution time can be attributed, satisfying part (a). However, part (b) is not genuinely realised: the only confounder-like column, priority_level, is simply a copy of a variable explicitly named in the query ('controlling for priority and category'). Category, the other query-named control, was not even added. Crucially, the system surfaced NO confounder from the data/text that was not already named in the query -- the decisive test for real causal reasoning fails. The remaining added columns are either the outcome restated (resolution_time_hours) or a collider (was_resolved), the latter being an outright adjustment error. Thus treatment structure is present but confounding control is weak and query-copied, yielding low confounder quality.
